parsed.explanation: The division is genuinely protective — public-accommodations law covering gender identity with an enforcement body, bias-crime enhancements, surgery-free marker changes, care-access shield, marriage recognition and a measured low trans-homicide rate — but the visitor passes through a hostile national regime first. National passport policy rejects X markers, consular cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex with a possible lifetime fraud finding, trans athletes are barred, and immigration custody is documented as abusive (forced labour, beatings, sexual assault). Facilities and care exposures are national but partly shielded locally. The combined regime is materially safer than the national line and materially less safe than a jurisdiction with an accepting border.

entry_documents.exposure: National policy bars X markers on new passports; consular cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and flags possible material-misrepresentation lifetime ineligibility; trans athletes banned; allied governments issued advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist; passport policy under active litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: A document discrepancy at the border can escalate to secondary screening, refusal, or immigration detention, moving the traveller into the custody regime.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. National prisons apply conversion-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal); trans prisoner counts no longer published.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State bias-crime enhancements, anti-discrimination enforcement and care-access orders apply locally, but no documented shield reaches national custody or immigration detention.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border-stage doubt feeds directly into the national detention system, where the division's protections do not operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities matching identity; 4 states criminalise bathroom use and a student was arrested; national facilities rules apply regardless of local law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No local facilities ban; division anti-discrimination law covers goods, services, facilities and lodging with an enforcement body able to grant relief; ranked in most-protective tier.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Locally congruent access is real, but national buildings and any federally operated setting follow the national rule.

care_services.exposure: National funding freeze, minors' care restrictions, proposed insurance bar for under-18 care, and subpoenas for records of patients under 19.
care_services.protection: State executive order directs agencies to protect gender-affirming care within its borders, expressly including people travelling in; local anti-discrimination coverage.
care_services.interaction: Care obtained inside the division is shielded; national insurers, federal facilities or record subpoenas crossing jurisdictions are not.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups among priorities; justice-department memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; schools investigated over social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same strategy disclaims targeting mere disagreement; local hate-crime statute covers gender identity and local police record gender X.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National framing raises official suspicion at the border and in federal investigations; local policing is comparatively protective.

minors_guardians.exposure: National order directs prosecution of teachers using a minor's preferred name; national care restrictions for minors; record subpoenas for under-19 patients.
minors_guardians.protection: Division shields gender-affirming care inside its borders and promotes inclusive school guidance; attorney general sued districts adopting outing policies.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family staying within the division is largely shielded on care and schools; federal actors and any out-of-division leg of the trip are not.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National bias-crime coverage is partial (23 states); general trans-homicide data exists nationally, though this division sits among the safest measured per-capita rates.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity bias enhancements, police gender-X data, licensing protections, panic-defence bar, and a documented low local rate.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local violence risk appears near baseline; the greater risk is official, at the border and in custody, not street predation.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No complaint or prosecution statistics for the gender-identity provisions of the anti-discrimination law; whether bias enhancements have been applied to a trans victim is unrecorded.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-rights body investigates and can grant relief; courts and an active legal-aid network; policy litigation ongoing.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local remedies are documented as available but their operation is unmeasured; national remedies for a visitor are largely absent.

anchor_checks.comparison: Veluna imposes an unremedied universal birth-sex facility rule with courts rejecting complaints. This division has no local facilities ban and an enforceable accommodation law, so it sits well above — the residual national facilities order is the only analogue, and local protection materially narrows it.

Teravi shows repeated hostile service treatment with partial mediation and a parent regime accepting documents. Here local service protections are stronger and violence data better, but the national border and custody exposure is worse than Teravi's accepting parent regime, holding this jurisdiction at a similar level.

Ilvora combines documented acceptance, working remedies and an accepting border. This division matches or exceeds it domestically, but national entry refusal risk, fraud findings and abusive immigration custody are documented hostile layers Ilvora lacks, placing it materially below.

parsed.synthesis: Inside the division the visitor meets functioning protection: accommodation law with an investigating agency, bias enhancements, easy documents, care-access shielding and low measured trans-homicide. That local layer cannot reach the national stage the traveller must pass through. Border screening rejects marker discrepancies and can produce refusal or a lifetime fraud finding; doubt at entry can lead into immigration custody with documented beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse, and national prisons apply conversion-style policies. Federal facilities bans and threat-framing rhetoric add background suspicion. The operative result is a protective destination behind a hostile gate: local everyday exposure is low, but the border and custody interaction drives the rating well below the division's own tier.
